note: Infrastructure overlaps with the follow-up report filed five days ago. Both use the same staging host; the TLS certificate serial is identical, which is what tied them together rather than the IP alone.

comment: Confident in the infrastructure attribution, less so in the targeting assessment — the victim set is inferred from two samples only.

note: Still responding on 443 as of this morning. Worth a sighting rather than expiry.

comment: The sender domain is a generic lookalike and the lure is off-the-shelf; this reads as commodity phishing rather than the actor named in the report.

note: Timeline reconstructed from the mail gateway and proxy logs. The three lures landed within 90 seconds of each other, which points at a scripted send rather than hand-picked targeting — the recipients share nothing but a public contact page.

comment: Low confidence in the TA542 label. The delivery chain resembles previous Emotet waves, but nothing here is infrastructure the group is known to own, and the loader host is a compromised third party. Treat the attribution as provisional until the C2 is tied to a known cluster.

note: Loader host is a legitimate WordPress site that was compromised, not attacker-owned. Notified the operator on the day of the incident; no response so far. Do not add to a permanent blocklist.
